readout_other: Ca2+ fluorescence microscopy; passive cavitation detection; mitochondrial viability fluorescence
direction_notes: Single 400 us pulses elicited Ca2+ responses in human neural cells: dispersed (cavitation-driven) below about 5 MHz and focal, propagating responses at 5.19 and 8.14 MHz.
safety_notes: Mitochondrial viability over 10 min after 8.14 MHz single-pulse FUS did not differ from sham (p = 0.235).

exposures.label: Single 400 us pulse FUS at 0.73-8.14 MHz on human neural cell culture

target.label: in vitro human neural cells (2D network)

device.model: homemade single-element spherical ceramic transducer (C-21, Fuji Ceramics Corp.), 15 mm diameter and focal length

timing.protocol_description: Single 400 us pulse (amplitude-modulated continuous sinusoid) at 0.73, 2.23, 5.19 or 8.14 MHz, triggered 10 s after the start of fluorescence recording; pressure escalated to find the minimum threshold at each frequency.

source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: FUS stimulations were performed using a homemade single-element prototype consisting of a spherical ceramic transducer (C-21, Fuji Ceramics Corp.) with a diameter and focal length of 15 mm, embedded using resin (Stycast 2850FT, Loctite) in a SLS 3D-printed nylon casing (PA12, Xometry Europe). A function generator (Tektronix AFG1062, Tektronix Inc.) and a 50 dB power amplifier (Kalmus 150 RF, Amplifier Research Modular RF) were used to drive the transducer at its fundamental frequency $( f _ { 1 } = 0 . 7 3$ MHz) or at its higher harmonics $( f _ { 3 } =$ 2.23 MHz, $f _ { 7 } = 5 . 1 9$ MHz and $f _ { 1 1 } = 8 . 1 4 \ : \mathrm { M H z } )$ .
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: The duration of the pulse was defined by amplitude-modulation with a 400 µs square-wave pulse.
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.model: FUS stimulations were performed using a homemade single-element prototype consisting of a spherical ceramic transducer (C-21, Fuji Ceramics Corp.)
